title: Tighten sufficient Clifford Gram conditioning from 807 to 16471/40
body:
For every INTEGER width f>=10 in the full three-qubit Gaussian-dyadic Clifford alphabet, prove the sufficient normalized tensor-Gram interval

(405/16384) I <= H_f <= (1334151/131072) I,
condition(H_f) <= 16471/40 = 411.775 < 807.

This answers Nick Petalas #6794's second-class trace handoff. The new actual lift is g=(hS) tensor I4, h=(1+i)/2 [[1,1],[1,-1]], S=diag(1,i): trace4, cube -I, quotient order three on one symplectic plane. Exactly6/10 quadratic forms are fixed in the36/28 Arf orbits. The real-part fixed-space bound and exact phase-one character cancellation give T3/d in [-3/36,6/36] or [-5/28,10/28]. Individual fixed-space traces need not be real.

Three exact all-thirty-row inequalities plus feasible primal mixtures yield multiplicity-ratio intervals [2/7,2353/20] for N28 and [1,2621/36] for N36. Every displayed dual has zero transvection coefficient: the new order-three upper constraint alone supplies these bounds, while the matching primals also satisfy the old transvection slab.
